clue.text: Press reporting of male fashion

parts.note: a cove is old British slang for a man or chap
the rage is the current fashion or craze

explanation.surface: A newspaper's account of what men are wearing this season.
explanation.definitionFit: The amount and manner of press attention a story gets is its media coverage, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Cambridge college takes on new lecturer, a bold type

parts.note: Clare is a college of Cambridge University
a don is a university lecturer, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A Cambridge college hires a new teacher who turns out to be a daring sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes on' and 'a' are link words; 'a bold type' looks like a daring person but means a typeface.
explanation.definitionFit: Clarendon is a heavy, bold typeface used for emphasis and display printing.

clue.text: Saw short film about area of special interest

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece is placed round another

parts.note: vid is short for video, a film
a site is an area, as in a Site of Special Scientific Interest, a protected area in Britain

explanation.surface: Watched a brief film about a protected nature area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short film' means the word video cut short, not a brief movie; 'about' here wraps rather than meaning 'on the subject of'. Britain designates protected Sites of Special Scientific Interest.
explanation.definitionFit: To have visited somewhere is to have gone and seen it, so saw works in sentences like 'saw Paris'.

clue.text: Satnav device in computer?

definitions.meaning: something that plans your route, as a satellite navigation unit does
a networking device found with computers that forwards data between networks

explanation.definitionFit: Router literally means something that routes, and is also the name of a network device sending data between computers.

clue.text: Old lady finally worrying about a cruel jibe

indicators.note: finally means take the last letter of the word that follows

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a taunt is a cruel jibe

explanation.surface: An elderly woman at last fretting over a nasty insult.
explanation.definitionFit: A great-aunt belongs to an older generation, a parent's aunt, so an old lady in the family.

clue.text: Spectator perhaps obtained grub

parts.note: The Spectator is a British weekly magazine, so an example of a mag
obtained means got

explanation.surface: An onlooker managed to get something to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spectator' looks like an onlooker, but with its capital it is the British weekly magazine; 'perhaps' marks it as one example of a MAG.
explanation.definitionFit: A grub is an insect larva, and a fly's larva is exactly this wriggling creature.

clue.text: Monkey about during pantomime, missing beginning of song

indicators.note: during means within, so one piece is placed inside another
missing means lacking, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: a masque is a dramatic entertainment with masks and music, like a pantomime

indicators.note: beginning of means take the first letter of the word

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: A monkey messing around in a pantomime with no song at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Missing beginning of song' leaves MAQUE; 'about' looks like the monkey fooling around, but it is circa, and 'during' sets it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A macaque is a monkey, such as the rhesus or the Barbary ape.

clue.text: Think bubbly isn't for keeping inside bottle

indicators.note: something kept inside is held within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: to guess is to think or suppose

indicators.note: bubbly means fizzing and lively, so the letters are stirred up

explanation.surface: Thinking that champagne won't do as something to keep in the bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bubbly' looks like champagne and 'bottle' like its container; instead 'bubbly' stirs the letters of isn't into TSIN, held by 'for keeping inside'. Bottle is British slang for courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottle is British slang for courage or nerve, and gutsiness means much the same.

clue.text: Topless pin-up enthrals extremely lewd codger

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so one piece holds another inside
topless means losing its top, the first letter in a down answer

parts.note: a poster is a picture pinned up on a wall

indicators.note: extremely means take the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A dirty old man captivated by a picture of a topless model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topless' removes P from POSTER; 'extremely' gives L and D from lewd, which go inside OSTER.
explanation.definitionFit: An oldster is an old person, informally, so a codger is a synonym.

clue.text: Exam success (though not a first) for slow-witted person

indicators.note: without its first letter: the word for exam success loses its opening letter

parts.note: to pass is to succeed in an exam

explanation.surface: Someone who scraped through an exam without top honours is called a dimwit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not a first' plays on a first-class degree, but it tells you to drop the first letter of PASS.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone a donkey-like fool is a common insult for a stupid person.

clue.text: Wanting tuition at university, there's requirement to save money

indicators.note: to save is to hold something inside, so one word is kept within another

parts.note: a need is a requirement
a ducat was an old gold coin used across Europe

explanation.surface: Someone missing out on college because they must put money aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting' means lacking, not desiring; 'at' and 'there's' are link words, and 'to save' means keep inside, not put aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lacking schooling or instruction is without education, which is what wanting tuition means here.

clue.text: Request all competitors to keep out of trouble

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so one word goes inside another

parts.note: the entry for a race is the whole field of competitors
to eat someone, as in 'what's eating you?', is to trouble them

explanation.surface: Everyone in the contest is asked to stay out of mischief.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'keep out of trouble' as one phrase; in fact 'to keep' holds, and 'out of' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest plea, so a request is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Where wine is produced by one of five volunteers

parts.note: a quint is short for a quintuplet, one of five born together
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Wine made by one of five people who offered to help.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A quinta is a Portuguese wine estate or vineyard, especially in the port-producing Douro valley.

clue.text: Family men daughter notices

parts.note: ads, advertisements, are notices

explanation.surface: Fathers are noticed by their daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Fathers are men with families, so family men is a loose synonym.

clue.text: Told to take long, hard look where flight goes

indicators.note: told means said aloud, so the words sound like the answer

parts.note: to stare well is to take a long hard look at something

explanation.surface: Someone is told to examine something closely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests air travel, but it means a flight of stairs; 'to' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A stairwell is the vertical shaft in a building where a flight of stairs runs.

clue.text: They may work hand in glove

definitions.text: They may work hand in glove

parts.words: They may work hand in glove
parts.note: 'hand in glove' usually means in close collusion, but here it is literal: people whose hand is inside a glove puppet

explanation.surface: Partners who collaborate closely.
explanation.definitionFit: Glove puppets are worked by a hand placed inside them, so their operators literally work hand in glove.

clue.text: Member of UN team ignores one European leader at the start

indicators.note: ignoring something means leaving it out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: UN forces are sent as peacekeepers, and a peacemaker is one of them
E is the standard abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A UN soldier passes over a European who led the way at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader at the start' looks like wordplay asking for a first letter, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In a race, the pacemaker leads at the start to set a fast pace for the others.

clue.text: Type of work that has little standing

definitions.text: Type of work that has little standing

parts.words: Type of work that has little standing
parts.note: 'little standing' suggests low status, but literally it is work done sitting down

explanation.surface: A lowly job with little prestige.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedentary work is done sitting, such as at a desk, so it involves very little standing up.

clue.text: Drink with food after operation

parts.note: a nip is a small drink of spirits
and means with, joining things
tuck is British schoolchildren's slang for food, especially sweets and snacks

explanation.surface: Having a drink and a meal after surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' is a link word. TUCK is British school slang for snacks.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase is an informal name for cosmetic surgery that tightens the skin, so it is an operation.

clue.text: Resolve is what golfer needs on tee

definitions.meaning: to resolve a problem is to smooth it away
read cryptically: a golfer on the tee takes a club made of metal out of the bag

explanation.definitionFit: To iron out difficulties is to resolve them; cryptically, a golfer gets the iron out to tee off.

clue.text: Soldiers stopping homeless person getting a lift? Come off it!

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so one piece goes inside another
getting a lift means being raised up, so in a down answer the word reads upwards

parts.note: a nomad has no fixed home
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Troops halting a tramp who is thumbing a lift, told not to be ridiculous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting a lift' turns the homeless word upwards in this down answer, giving DAMON; 'stopping' plugs the soldiers into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dream on is a scornful phrase telling someone their hopes are unrealistic, just like come off it.

clue.text: 50% of undergraduates are upright

indicators.note: fifty per cent means half, so only the first half of the word is kept

parts.note: undergraduates are students

explanation.surface: Half the students are standing up.
explanation.walkthrough: Half of the eight-letter STUDENTS is its first four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In building, a stud is a vertical post in a timber-framed wall, so an upright.

clue.text: Husband abandons the country with a will

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving behind, so a letter is removed

parts.note: a state is a country

explanation.surface: A husband leaves the country with determination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With a will' looks like 'determinedly', but it means having left a legal will.
explanation.definitionFit: Testate describes someone who died having made a valid legal will.

clue.text: CD available without charge, ready to be dispatched

indicators.note: without means outside, an old sense, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: taken as written as two letters
a rate is a charge or price

explanation.surface: A compact disc offered free and ready to post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without charge' looks like 'free', but 'without' means outside; 'available' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods packed in crates are ready for shipping, so crated means ready to be dispatched.

clue.text: Seizing ball, was desperately anxious briefly for goal

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold of, so one piece is put inside another
briefly means shortened, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to burn is to be consumed with intense feeling, so burned means was desperately anxious
a ball is round, like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone frantic with worry grabs the ball and goes for goal, as in football.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' cuts BURNED to BURNE, and 'Seizing' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Bourne is an archaic word for a destination or limit, as in Hamlet's undiscovered country 'from whose bourn no traveller returns'.

clue.text: Naughty child not a single teacher kept back and put in detention

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child

indicators.note: kept back means turned to face the other way, so the words are read in reverse

parts.note: no means not a single, as in 'no one'
sir is how British pupils address a male teacher

explanation.surface: A badly behaved pupil, with no teacher around, ends up in detention after school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kept back' turns NO + SIR into RISON.
explanation.definitionFit: To imprison is to confine or detain someone, so put in detention is a synonym.

clue.text: Kind of trade which gives top men rake-off

indicators.note: off means wrong or not right, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A trading arrangement that gives senior executives a cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rake-off' looks like a cut of the profits, but 'rake' is part of the anagram and 'off' signals it.
explanation.definitionFit: Trade carried out freely with no restrictions on who can buy and sell is a type of commerce.

clue.text: Sandra regularly used as name for girl

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Sandra keeps being used as a girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ada is a girl's first name, as in Ada Lovelace.

clue.text: Play for time no end, governing as dictator

indicators.note: with no end means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to stall is to play for time
a party in power is in, so in means governing

explanation.surface: A leader deliberately stalling while ruling as a tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No end' cuts STALL to STAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalin ruled the Soviet Union as an absolute dictator from the 1920s to 1953.

clue.text: Dickensian character, prisoner of dull toil

indicators.note: a prisoner is held inside, so one piece is put inside another

parts.note: dry means dull or boring
Barnaby Rudge is the title character of a Charles Dickens novel

explanation.surface: A Dickens character trapped in dreary, back-breaking labour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dickensian character' tempts with famous names like Fagin; it is the less obvious Barnaby, from the novel named after him, and 'prisoner of' holds him.
explanation.definitionFit: Drudgery is hard, monotonous work, so toil is a synonym.
